claim.pdf_says: In Format 1 the words GREATER, LESS and EQUAL are UNDERLINED; IS, THAN and TO are printed without an underline, and the relational characters '>', '<', '=' carry no underline.
claim.markdown_says:
| IS GREATER THAN       |
| IS >                  |
| IS LESS THAN          |
| IS <                  |
| IS EQUAL TO           |
| IS =                  |   (no underlining anywhere, and no 'Figure notes' paragraph for this figure)
claim.why_it_matters: Underlined words in a general format are KEYWORDS (required); non-underlined uppercase words are OPTIONAL words. With the underlining dropped and no Figure notes paragraph to record it, the markdown gives no way to derive that 'IS' and 'THAN'/'TO' are optional while GREATER/LESS/EQUAL are required. Every other figure in this transcription records this (225 'Figure notes' blockquotes exist; page 223 even preserves inline underlining as '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1'), so this figure is an outlier.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sides by independent inspection. PDF: rendered specs page 203 at 300 dpi and cropped the 8.7.5.1 Format 1 figure at 3x. The printed glyphs are unambiguous - each of the six alternatives begins with 'IS' set WITHOUT an underline, and the underline rules sit under GREATER, under LESS, and under EQUAL only; THAN and TO are un-underlined; the '>' , '<' and '=' rows carry no rule. MARKDOWN: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8829-8840 (workunit page-203.md) contain the figure as a plain fenced ASCII box with zero underline markup, and lines 8842-8896 confirm no 'Figure notes' blockquote follows either Format 1 or Format 2 of 8.7.5 - the next content is 8.7.5.2 Syntax rules. The quoted markdown text matches the file byte-for-byte, so the claim does not misquote either source, and the loss is not reflow, page-break furniture, or hyphenation.

The loss IS normative and is not recoverable from the surrounding markdown. The transcription itself carries the metalanguage that makes underlining load-bearing: 5.2.2 Keywords - 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats ... They are required in order to select the functionality' (line 2628); 5.2.3 Optional words - 'shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats ... may be written to add clarity' (line 2641); restated at 8.3.2.4.2/8.3.2.4.3 (lines 5770, 5805). Underlining is therefore the SOLE carrier of the keyword-vs-optional-word distinction inside a general format. Stripped of it, the figure cannot yield the fact that 'A > B', 'A GREATER B' and 'A IS GREATER THAN B' are all legal while 'A THAN B' is not, and 8.7.5.2's abbreviation rules (lines 8874-8894) do not supply it - they only equate '>' with 'GREATER THAN'.

Where the claim is WRONG is its outlier argument, which I checked mechanically and refuted: of the 514 fenced figures in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, only 214 are followed by a 'Figure notes' blockquote and ZERO contain <u> markup, leaving 300 fenced figures with no underline information at all. The 97 <u> lines (including the page-223 '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1' the claim cites) are all inline single-line formats that are not inside code fences, so they are a different representation, not a precedent this fenced figure departs from. Page 203's figure is one of 300 in the same condition, not an anomaly - the finding is a systemic transcription gap that happens to bite here, and any fix should be scoped as such rather than as a one-off page repair.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, but mis-scoped and mis-motivated by the original claim.

The content loss: in ISO/IEC 1989:2023 clause 8.7.5.1 Format 1 (simple-relational-operator), printed on PDF page 203, the standard underlines GREATER, LESS and EQUAL (keywords, required per 5.2.2) and leaves IS, THAN and TO un-underlined (optional words per 5.2.3). specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8831-8840 transcribe the figure with no underline markup and no 'Figure notes' blockquote, so the keyword/optional-word split - the only thing that makes 'A > B' and 'A GREATER B' derivable as legal - is unrecoverable from the figure.

Three corrections to the claim:

1. NOT an outlier. 300 of the 514 fenced figures in the transcription carry neither <u> markup nor a Figure notes blockquote (only 214 have notes; no fenced block anywhere uses <u>). The 97 <u> occurrences, including page 223's '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1', are inline non-fenced one-line formats - a different container, not a convention this figure violates. Treat this as one instance of a systemic gap, not a page-203 defect.

2. The same clause's Format 2 (extended-relational-operator), printed on PDF page 204 and transcribed at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8855-8868, has the identical loss: the print underlines NOT, GREATER, LESS, EQUAL and OR while leaving IS, THAN and TO bare. A fix that touches only Format 1 leaves 8.7.5.1 half-repaired.

3. The un-underlined '>', '<', '=' are NOT part of the defect and must not be recorded as optional. Line 2728 (5.2.5) states that special character words and separators appearing in formats are required even though not underlined. The claim reports their lack of underline accurately but a careless remediation could invert their status.

Secondary, same figure: the printed outer delimiter in both formats is a single large pair of CURLY BRACES - a required choice, exactly one alternative selected (5.2.6) - with no '|' choice-indicator bars inside either figure. The markdown renders Format 1 as corner glyphs ('⌐ ¬' over 'L ┘') and Format 2 as a box-drawing rectangle ('┌─┐' over '└─┘'); neither conveys brace-versus-bracket, so the required-choice semantics is also not derivable. No choice indicator was lost, because none is printed.
